market.title: EU Mandates Instant Payments for All SEPA Transactions
market.summary_short: New EU regulation requires all SEPA credit transfers to be processed instantly by early 2027, impacting banks and corporates across Europe. This includes mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) for fraud prevention.
market.summary_detail: The European Parliament has formally adopted the Instant Payments Regulation, making instant credit transfers mandatory and free of charge for all euro transactions within the SEPA zone. This regulation, expected to enter into force in early 2027, aims to modernize the European payment landscape, ensuring funds are available to recipients within seconds, 24/7/365. Banks must offer instant payments at the same or lower cost as traditional SEPA credit transfers. A crucial component is the mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP), requiring payment service providers to verify the payee's identity to mitigate fraud risks associated with real-time transactions. This represents a significant shift for financial institutions and corporate treasuries, demanding substantial IT infrastructure upgrades and process adjustments.
key_points: Mandatory instant payments for all SEPA euro credit transfers.
Funds available within 10 seconds, 24/7/365.
Pricing must be equal to or lower than standard SEPA credit transfers.
Includes mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) for fraud prevention.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for CMIplus, requiring immediate focus on full compliance and enhancement of instant payment capabilities across all CEE network banks. The VoP mandate necessitates integration with national VoP schemes or development of proprietary solutions to protect clients from fraud in real-time environments. CMIplus must ensure seamless, cost-effective instant payment processing and robust fraud prevention tools.

market.title: ISO 20022 Migration Accelerates, EBICS 3.0 Adoption Critical
market.summary_short: The global migration to ISO 20022 for cross-border payments is progressing, with banks and corporates urged to finalize their transition plans. EBICS 3.0 is becoming the standard for secure corporate-to-bank communication.
market.summary_detail: The SWIFT CBPR+ migration to ISO 20022 is nearing its final stages, with many financial institutions already live with the new standard for cross-border payments. Corporates are increasingly adopting ISO 20022 for domestic and international payments, leveraging its rich data capabilities for better reconciliation and treasury management. Concurrently, the adoption of EBICS 3.0 is gaining momentum, particularly in Germany and Austria, offering enhanced security, multi-bank capabilities, and support for ISO 20022 XML messages. This dual shift requires corporates to update their ERP/TMS systems and banking interfaces to ensure seamless communication and data exchange. Banks are investing heavily in infrastructure to support these standards, providing advanced APIs and H2H connections.

Beyond basic account information and payment initiation, banks are offering a wider array of APIs for services like virtual accounts, cash pooling, FX trading, and liquidity management. This allows corporate treasuries to achieve greater automation, real-time visibility into cash positions across multiple banks and currencies, and more efficient reconciliation. The shift towards API-driven treasury operations reduces manual effort, improves data accuracy, and enables more sophisticated cash forecasting and risk management. Companies are increasingly seeking banks that provide comprehensive API catalogs and robust developer support.

market.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation: CEE Banks Accelerate Adoption
market.summary_short: The EU's new Instant Payments Regulation mandates banks to offer instant credit transfers in EUR, with strict deadlines and fee restrictions. This regulation aims to make instant payments the norm across the Eurozone and beyond.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, which entered into force in April 2024, requires all payment service providers (PSPs) in the EU and EEA to offer instant credit transfers in EUR. A key provision is that instant payments cannot be charged at a higher fee than traditional SEPA credit transfers. This regulation is set to significantly impact corporate cash management by accelerating payment cycles, improving liquidity, and enabling real-time treasury operations. CEE banks, while often early adopters of digital solutions, face the challenge of upgrading legacy systems and ensuring interoperability across diverse national infrastructures.

thought.title: AI Governance Becomes Critical for Trust and Compliance in Banking
thought.summary_short: The rapid adoption of AI in financial services necessitates robust governance frameworks to manage risks, ensure ethical use, and comply with emerging regulations. Banks must develop clear strategies for AI explainability, fairness, and data privacy.
thought.summary_detail: As financial institutions increasingly deploy AI for fraud detection, credit scoring, personalized services, and operational efficiency, regulators are intensifying scrutiny on AI governance. Firms must establish comprehensive frameworks addressing data quality, model validation, ethical considerations, and accountability. The focus will be on ensuring AI systems are transparent, explainable, fair, and non-discriminatory, while also protecting customer data. Proactive AI governance is crucial not only for regulatory compliance but also for building and maintaining customer trust in an AI-driven financial landscape, particularly when integrating third-party AI solutions.
key_points: Regulators are increasing focus on AI governance, ethics, and explainability.
Banks must establish frameworks for data quality, model validation, and accountability.
Ensuring AI systems are transparent, fair, and non-discriminatory is paramount.
Proactive governance builds trust and ensures compliance with evolving AI regulations.
thought.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus should evaluate AI applications for enhanced fraud detection, payment analytics, and client servicing, ensuring robust AI governance. This includes assessing third-party AI tools for compliance and integrating ethical AI principles into platform development and data utilization.

thought.title: Stablecoins: Disruptive Potential for Payments and Treasury

Financial institutions must make bold strategic choices to navigate their emergence, which could fundamentally reshape global payment systems and corporate treasury functions. This disruption necessitates a re-evaluation of existing payment product development strategies and potentially transformative changes to operating models to either integrate stablecoin-related services or effectively compete with stablecoin-based transactions, particularly impacting multi-currency payments and liquidity management.
key_points: Stablecoins are a significant disruptive force for banks in 2026.
Requires strategic choices and adaptation from financial institutions.
Impacts payment product development and operating models.
Potential to reshape multi-currency payments and treasury functions.

Assess the feasibility of integrating stablecoin-related services or offering advisory to corporates on managing stablecoin exposures, which could impact multi-currency cash pooling, FX, and real-time treasury.

regulatory.title: TARGET Services: Ongoing Governance and Professional Use Updates

The ECB continuously oversees their governance, ensuring stability, efficiency, and resilience. Regular updates to 'TARGET professional use documents & links' provide essential operational and technical guidance for participants. Financial institutions, particularly those involved in high-value and instant Euro payments, must actively monitor these updates to ensure ongoing operational compliance, efficient liquidity management, and seamless integration with the evolving TARGET ecosystem.

Regular updates to TARGET professional use documents and links.
Ensuring stability, efficiency, and resilience of core payment infrastructures.
Requires active monitoring by financial institutions for operational compliance.

regulatory.title: EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 released, effective January 2027
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has updated its Fraud Taxonomy to version 7.0, incorporating the latest fraud trends and effective 1 January 2027. This update aims to harmonise fraud data classification and improve information sharing, particularly under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on 1 January 2027. This annual review, supported by fraud experts across Europe, ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends. Key updates include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with three specific modi ('support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', 'charity / donation fraud') and adding new labels for 'suspected money mule activity' and 'card chip relay'. The taxonomy provides a harmonised pan-European vocabulary for describing and categorising payment fraud scenarios, including card transactions. It is designed to enhance fraud monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, explicitly supporting data classification for arrangements under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (likely PSD3/PSR).
key_points: EBA Fraud Taxonomy updated to version 7.0.
Effective date for implementation: 2027-01-01.
New fraud modi: 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', 'charity / donation fraud'.
Supports data classification for the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSD3/PSR).
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must review the updated EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 to ensure its internal fraud monitoring, reporting, and data classification systems are aligned. This includes updating fraud detection rules and categories within CMIplus to comply with the new definitions by the effective date. Proactive preparation for data sharing requirements under the future Payment Services Regulation is also advised.

regulatory.title: EBA report explores Agentic AI's impact on embedded finance
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA's Open Finance Working Group published a report on 'Supercharging embedded finance with agentic AI,' identifying key use cases and future roles for financial institutions. This report provides strategic insights into leveraging AI within Open Banking frameworks.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) published a new report by its Open Finance Working Group (OFWG) titled “Supercharging embedded finance with agentic AI” on 10 June 2026. This report aims to identify specific use cases within embedded finance where the application of agentic AI could bring significant benefits to financial institutions. It outlines the potential impact of agentic AI on critical areas of embedded finance and delineates evolving roles for financial institutions in this landscape. While not a direct regulatory mandate, the report serves as crucial thought leadership, informing the strategic direction for banks in the context of Open Banking and the anticipated expansion into Open Finance (e.g., FIDA).
key_points: Report published by EBA's Open Finance Working Group.
Focuses on leveraging agentic AI in embedded finance.
Identifies use cases and future roles for financial institutions.
Informs strategic development in Open Banking/Open Finance.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) should review this report to understand potential strategic opportunities and future technological requirements for integrating AI into its Open Banking APIs and embedded finance offerings. This includes evaluating how agentic AI could enhance corporate treasury services, liquidity management, and real-time payment solutions, preparing for potential future regulatory guidance or standards in this evolving area.
